title: Schema Signal Fusion and Schema Delta Score (SDS) for Structured Output Quality
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We see intermittent structured-output (JSON) anomalies after model/config changes that escape field-level schema checks and result in subtle quality regressions (mis-typed fields, field value semantic shifts, and optional-field omission). Existing detectors generate many false positives when field value distributions shift slowly.

Goal: Build a fused signal detector that combines schema validation, token-level model confidence signals, per-field distribution drift, and mutation-based synthetic tests into a single actionable score: the Schema Delta Score (SDS). SDS should enable: 1) earlier detection of quality regressions tied to model/config changes; 2) high-precision alerts for rollouts (canary gating); 3) prioritized investigation hints (root-cause cues).
acceptance_criteria: SDS computes per-rollout and per-model-variant score and stores time-series in metrics backend
Canary gating integration: SDS >= threshold  triggers canary pause and creates rollback suggestion
False positive rate on historical rollouts reduced by >= 40% vs current per-field rule alerts
Alert payload includes top-3 contributing signals and example sample pairs (baseline vs candidate)
Dashboard panel shows per-field SDS breakdown and 'signal fusion' contribution bars
implementation_steps: Instrument three base signals: (A) strict JSON schema violations (structural), (B) per-field distribution shift using population embeddings and KS-like metrics (semantic drift), (C) token-level softmax and generation-alignment confidence delta from baseline model
Define normalization for each base signal and map to 0..1 anomaly score; design temporal smoothing window (default 1h) and bootstrap baseline windows
Build the SDS aggregator: weighted fusion with adjustable weights per-organization; default weights: structural 0.5, semantic 0.3, confidence 0.2
Add synthetic mutation harness: generate controlled mutations for a subset of prompts (schema-preserving/value-swapped/omission) and compute sensitivity to simulate regressions
Create canary hook: evaluate SDS on canary traffic and block rollouts when SDS > canary_threshold (default 0.6), with auto-notification to runbooks
Persist SDS time-series to metrics backend and expose via Console dashboard and alerting rules
Add PRD + design review and run small shadow traffic experiment for 2 weeks before enabling hard gating
design_decisions: Use fusion instead of single-rule alerting to reduce noise from slow distributional shifts
Keep structural schema validator as highest-priority signal but allow user-configurable weight; structural violations still produce immediate high-severity alerts
Implement mutation harness as 'synthetic probes' that run in parallel to production inference to test brittleness without impacting latency
Expose both global SDS and per-field SDS so teams can triage by affected fields and signals
risks: SDS may still miss subtle semantic regressions if baseline probes are not representative; risk mitigated by expanding probe sets iteratively
Metric explosion: storing per-field SDS for high-cardinality schemas will increase storage and dashboard complexity
Ops complexity: default thresholds might not generalize across customers and will require tuning for high-sensitivity workloads
False sense of safety if teams over-rely on SDS and disable manual sample review
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (shadow-only, 2 weeks): compute SDS for all rollouts, log alerts to internal channel only
Phase 2 (canary advisory, 3 weeks): enable SDS-based advisory alerts for selected customers; collect feedback and tune weights/thresholds
Phase 3 (soft gating, 2 weeks): enable pause-on-canary when SDS > threshold for internal deployments; require manual approval to proceed
Phase 4 (opt-in hard gating): expose gating toggle to Dedicated/Private tenants; default off for hosted until stable metrics observed
metrics: SDS_per_field: top N field scores with contribution breakdown
Precision_reduction: percent decrease in false-positive alerts vs baseline rule alerts
Mean_time_to_detect: comparison of SDS vs current rule-based detection
Canary_block_rate: fraction of canaries paused by SDS gating
